questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 13 cm and a height of 10 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 13 × 10 = 65 cm². Say the ½ out loud before multiplying so you never skip halving.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A student's business plan lists 'our founder ran a café for five years' as a strength. Which section of the plan does this belong in?
questions.why: Founder experience is a strength, so it belongs in the SWOT analysis, not the market analysis (which studies customers and competitors), the executive summary (a one-page overview), or the financial plan (costs and revenue).

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Freud's model, which part is entirely unconscious and never becomes rational?
questions.why: The id is wholly unconscious, driven by instinct and pleasure, unlike the ego, which is partly conscious and deals with reality.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a sealed container, 25g of reactants react fully. What is the mass of the products?
questions.why: Mass is conserved in a closed system, so the products must total 25g — nothing can enter or escape.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What word describes a solid that suddenly appears when two liquids react?
questions.why: A precipitate is the solid that forms when two solutions react, showing a chemical change has occurred.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Lord of the Flies, why does Jack paint his face before hunting?
questions.answer: It hides his identity and shame
questions.why: The face-paint acts as a mask, freeing Jack from guilt and civilised restraint, letting his savage side take over more easily.
options: It hides his identity and shame
It helps him see in the dark

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A bakery sells cakes and also offers cake-decorating classes. The classes are best described as a…
questions.why: A service is work or skill provided to a customer, like teaching a class. A product is a physical item, like a cake, that the customer takes home.
